docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: Meta's advertising franchise, segment economics and control
Source: compiled from: https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2025/Meta-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Results/default.aspx; https://s21.q4cdn.com/399680738/files/doc_financials/2025/q3/META-Q3-2025-Prepared-Remarks.pdf
Date: 2025-10-29

Meta operates Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp within Family of Apps (FoA). Its second segment, Reality Labs (RL), develops virtual, augmented and mixed-reality hardware, software and content. The financial engine is advertising against attention on the apps; hardware and other activities account for a much smaller revenue stream. The following figures are from the October 29 results, in millions of dollars.

| Q3 2025 | Revenue | Operating income |
|---|---:|---:|
| Advertising | 50,082 | Not separately disclosed |
| FoA other revenue | 690 | Not separately disclosed |
| FoA total | 50,772 | 24,967 |
| Reality Labs | 470 | (4,432) |
| Consolidated | 51,242 | 20,535 |

FoA's operating margin is 49.2%, calculated from these reported figures; consolidated margin is 40%. Removing RL from a valuation is an analytical sensitivity, not a claim that those losses are eliminated or available to shareholders. In the first nine months, RL lost $13,171 million against revenue of $1,252 million. Founder Mark Zuckerberg remains CEO; Susan Li is CFO. The Q3 diluted weighted-average share count was 2,572 million, versus 2,600 million a year earlier. That is an EPS denominator, not the exact November 3 common shares outstanding. Headcount was 78,450, up 8%.

Scale is visible in family daily active people of 3.54 billion in September, up 8%. Zuckerberg said Instagram reached 3 billion monthly actives and Threads exceeded 150 million daily actives. These are different metrics and cannot be added together. Advertising growth reflects both more impressions and better pricing: Q3 impressions rose 14%, while average price per ad rose 10%. More audience engagement creates additional inventory; relevance and measured conversion can make each impression more valuable to advertisers.

The moat hypothesis is a reinforcing combination of audience, creators, advertiser access and recommendation quality. It is not immunity from competition or changes in mobile operating-system policies. Meta itself identifies dependency on third-party data signals, privacy restrictions and regulation as risks. Nor does audience scale prove that frontier-model investment will earn an attractive return.

Management says its AI investments are already improving recommendations and ads. The same management is committing substantial resources to less proven products and frontier research. Governance therefore matters: investors are underwriting capital allocation as well as current app profitability. Exact voting-control percentages, individual insider ownership and independent-director evaluations are not supplied by these earnings materials and are not assumed here.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Three fiscal years and the latest quarter
Source: compiled from: https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2023/Meta-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2022-Results/default.aspx; https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2025/Meta-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2024-Results; https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2025/Meta-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Results/default.aspx
Date: 2025-10-29

Dollar amounts below are millions, except diluted EPS. Annual observations come from releases dated February 1, 2023 and January 29, 2025; quarter and nine-month observations were released October 29, 2025. The 2023 annual comparison is the prior-year column of the January 2025 release, not a subsequently reconstructed fiscal year.

| Metric | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | Q3 2025 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 116,609 | 134,902 | 164,501 | 51,242 |
| Revenue growth | (1%) | 15.7% calculated | 22% | 26% |
| Operating income | 28,944 | 46,751 | 69,380 | 20,535 |
| Operating margin | 25% | 35% | 42% | 40% |
| Diluted EPS, GAAP | 8.59 | 14.87 | 23.86 | 1.05 |
| Operating cash flow | 50,475 | 71,113 | 91,328 | 29,999 |
| Capex including finance-lease principal | 32,036 | 28,103 | 39,225 | 19,374 |
| Free cash flow | 18,439 | 43,010 | 52,103 | 10,625 |
| Cash and marketable securities, period end | 40,738 | 65,403 | 77,815 | 44,448 |
| Long-term debt, period end | 9,923 | 18,385 | 28,826 | 28,834 |

Capex includes equipment purchases plus finance-lease principal to preserve the company's free-cash-flow definition. It is not interchangeable with property purchases alone. Q3 property purchases were $18,829 million and lease principal was $545 million. For the first nine months, operating cash flow was $79,586 million, property purchases $48,308 million, lease principal $1,770 million and FCF $29,508 million, versus $38,951 million in the comparable 2024 period. Thus cash generation is strong before investment, but rising reinvestment is already reducing cash available after investment.

Net cash excluding leases was $15,614 million at September 30, calculated as cash and securities less long-term debt. This simplified measure excludes lease commitments and other liabilities. It is not a comprehensive net financial obligation calculation.

Q3 share repurchases were $3.16 billion and dividends/dividend equivalents $1.33 billion. FY2024 repurchases were $29.75 billion and dividends/dividend equivalents $5.072 billion. Buybacks must be considered alongside stock compensation: Q3 share-based compensation was $5,555 million. A repurchase dollar does not necessarily reduce share count dollar-for-dollar.

The quarter's $1.05 GAAP EPS includes the $15.93 billion noncash tax charge. The company separately gives $7.25 excluding that charge. Neither number should be annualized mechanically. ROIC under a consistent invested-capital definition is not available in these releases; no synthetic ROIC is assigned.
docs.D03_latest_results_and_guidance.md:
Title: October 29 earnings — ad strength versus infrastructure commitments
Source: compiled from: https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2025/Meta-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Results/default.aspx; https://s21.q4cdn.com/399680738/files/doc_financials/2025/q3/META-Q3-2025-Prepared-Remarks.pdf
Date: 2025-10-29

Q3 revenue of $51.24 billion rose 26%, or 25% in constant currency. Advertising revenue was $50.082 billion, also up 26%. Operating income rose 18% to $20.535 billion, slower than sales as expenses rose 32% to $30.707 billion. Margin fell from 43% to 40%. These operating results are separate from the tax item that reduced net earnings.

The One Big Beautiful Bill Act produced an unusual distinction between tax accounting and cash taxes. Meta expects a significant reduction in US federal cash tax payments, but recognition of a valuation allowance against deferred tax assets generated a one-time, noncash $15.93 billion charge. Reported effective tax rate was 87%, net income $2.709 billion and diluted EPS $1.05. Excluding the charge, management reports a 14% rate, $18.64 billion net income and $7.25 EPS. The charge is not an operating cash outflow of $15.93 billion.

| October 29 outlook | Management forecast |
|---|---|
| Q4 revenue | $56–59 billion |
| Q4 currency effect | Approximately 1% revenue-growth tailwind |
| FY2025 total expenses | $116–118 billion, previously $114–118 billion |
| FY2025 capex including leases | $70–72 billion, previously $66–72 billion |
| Q4 tax rate absent landscape changes | 12–15% |

The pivotal statement is about 2026, for which a specific capex dollar range is not provided: “capital expenditures dollar growth will be notably larger in 2026 than 2025.” Management also expects expenses to grow at a significantly faster percentage rate, driven primarily by infrastructure costs, cloud expenses and depreciation, then employee compensation. This is not merely a higher cash-investment budget: it creates future income-statement costs.

Zuckerberg describes the strategy as aggressively front-loading capacity for optimistic AI timelines. His fallback is also explicit: “in the worst case, we would just slow building new infrastructure for some period while we grow into what we've built.” That option may reduce future incremental spending; it does not recover sunk capital.

Near-term evidence for monetization includes AI recommendation improvements generating 5% more time on Facebook and 10% on Threads; Instagram video time rose more than 30% year over year. Reels' annual revenue run rate exceeded $50 billion, while annualized spending through end-to-end AI ad tools exceeded $60 billion. These are management run-rate metrics, not additive new revenue categories. No 2026 operating-income floor or peak-Reality-Labs-loss commitment is in this October outlook.
docs.D04_price_and_valuation.md:
Title: November 3 market snapshot and valuation bridge
Source: compiled from: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/META/history/?period1=1761868800&period2=1762214400; https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/stocks/roth-mkm-keeps-their-buy-rating-on-meta-platforms-meta-1035390210; https://insight.factset.com/sp-500-earnings-season-update-october-31-2025; https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2025/Meta-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Results/default.aspx; https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2025/Meta-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2024-Results
Date: 2025-11-03

The historical daily price record reports an unadjusted November 3 close of $637.71, an open of $656.00, high $659.33, low $636.18 and volume of 33,003,600 shares. October 31 closed at $648.35 on 56,953,200 shares. Only these historical rows are used; present-day quote widgets and dividend-adjusted prices incorporating subsequent dividends are excluded.

An October 16 TipRanks report carried by Markets Insider gives a one-year high of $796.25 and low of $479.80, and average volume of 12 million. Those are dated October 16 observations, not a newly verified November 3 rolling range. November 3's close is 19.9% below that already-observed high, a calculation of 637.71/796.25−1. It is 15.2% below the $751.67 October 29 close reported in historical market data. Do not confuse the peak drawdown with the one-day earnings reaction.

Exact cutoff common shares and a contemporaneous market-cap feed were not authenticated. Multiplying the quarter's 2.517 billion basic weighted-average shares by the close gives an explicitly illustrative equity-value proxy of $1.605 trillion; this is not exact market capitalization. Using $15.614 billion net cash excluding leases gives an illustrative enterprise-value proxy of $1.589 trillion.

A transparent trailing earnings bridge is preferable to importing an undated forward multiple. FY2024 EPS $23.86 less nine-month 2024 EPS $15.88 plus nine-month 2025 EPS $14.62 produces approximate trailing GAAP EPS of $22.60; adding back the disclosed $6.20 tax-charge impact gives $28.80. Share-denominator changes mean this sum-of-quarter/period bridge is approximate. Corresponding calculated P/Es at the close are 28.2x GAAP and 22.1x tax-normalized trailing earnings. RL losses remain in both earnings measures.

Trailing FCF is $52.103 billion−$38.951 billion+$29.508 billion=$42.660 billion. Against the equity-value proxy, the calculated trailing FCF yield is 2.7%. Higher capex makes that a materially different signal from tax-normalized P/E.

FactSet's October 31 report puts S&P 500 forward twelve-month P/E at 22.9x, versus five- and ten-year averages of 19.9x and 18.6x. Verified November 3 Meta forward consensus EPS, consensus EPS growth, forward P/E, EV/EBITDA and its own consistent five-to-ten-year multiple range are not available in this snapshot. In particular, a roughly 20x valuation at a different trading date must not be relabeled as November 3 market data.
docs.D05_market_worries.md:
Title: The contemporary bear case — spending returns, not an advertising collapse
Source: compiled from: https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/30/meta-stock-earnings-ai-spend.html; https://www.reuters.com/business/metas-profit-hit-by-16-billion-one-time-tax-charge-2025-10-29/; https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2025/Meta-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Results/default.aspx
Date: 2025-10-30

CNBC's Samantha Subin, October 30, reported Meta's worst one-day share performance since October 2022, with the shares down more than 11%. The article describes “skepticism about the payoff from its aggressive artificial intelligence spending plans” overshadowing strong results. The dated report is about the investment-return debate, not evidence that the app revenue engine has stopped growing.

Reuters' October 29 report, updated October 30, was headed “Meta forecasts bigger capital costs next year as Zuckerberg lays out aggressive AI buildout.” It highlights the larger 2026 capital program and the fact that Q3 cost growth exceeded revenue growth. Those are observable points of pressure: expenses up 32%, sales up 26%, and operating margin down three percentage points. A sustainable business can still be overpriced if maintenance needs, competitive research spending or depreciation consume too much of its growth.

The bear argument has three components. First, useful ad-ranking improvements may not justify the entire frontier-AI budget. Second, if competitors all add capacity, compute returns can fall even while usage rises. Third, compensation, depreciation and cloud commitments can lag spending decisions, so today's operating margin may not represent mature economics. These are analytical interpretations of the disclosed commitments, not verbatim analyst quotations.

CNBC quotes Zuckerberg: “It's pretty early, but I think we're seeing the returns in the core business.” He also says those returns create confidence that Meta should invest more and avoid underinvestment. Investors must assess how much of the budget supports already monetizing recommendations and advertising, versus speculative new models, consumer assistants and devices.

Reality Labs is a separate source of concern: $4.432 billion lost in Q3, against only $470 million revenue. It would be misleading either to ignore those losses or to treat their indefinite continuation as established fact. Management's capital-allocation willingness, rather than accounting presentation alone, determines whether an ex-RL valuation is realizable.

Regulatory risk is not just theoretical in the earnings outlook. Meta warns EU changes to its Less Personalized Ads offering could materially affect European revenue as early as Q4. It also identifies US youth-related trials scheduled for 2026 that could create material losses. Neither outcome is resolved at the cutoff. The $15.93 billion tax charge is another headline concern, but its noncash nature and projected cash-tax reduction distinguish it from recurring operating deterioration.
docs.D06_peers_and_industry.md:
Title: Alphabet and Amazon — competing platforms and investment intensity
Source: compiled from: https://s206.q4cdn.com/479360582/files/doc_news/2025/Oct/29/attachments/2025q3-alphabet-earnings-release.pdf; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872425000121/amzn-20250930xex991.htm; https://www.cnbc.com/2025/10/30/meta-stock-earnings-ai-spend.html; https://www.macrotrends.net/stocks/charts/GOOGL/alphabet/pe-ratio
Date: 2025-10-30

Alphabet and Amazon provide useful benchmarks, but neither is a pure comparable. Alphabet combines search, YouTube, cloud and other activities. Amazon combines retail, seller services, advertising and AWS. Meta is much more concentrated in advertising and funds RL from app profits. Comparing consolidated margins without this mix distinction can produce a false conclusion about competitive strength.

| Latest reported quarter | Revenue | Reported growth | Operating income | Operating margin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Meta, October 29 release | $51.242bn | 26% | $20.535bn | 40% reported |
| Alphabet, October 29 release | $102.346bn | 16% | $31.228bn | 31% reported |
| Amazon, October 30 release | $180.2bn | 13% | $17.4bn | 9.7% calculated |

Alphabet's operating income includes a $3.457 billion European Commission fine. Its earnings release reports diluted EPS of $2.87 and net income $34.979 billion, with $12.759 billion other income. Those items are reasons not to equate reported EPS growth with recurring operating growth. Amazon's operating income includes $2.5 billion for an FTC legal settlement and $1.8 billion estimated severance costs. Management says operating income without those charges would be $21.7 billion. AWS revenue increased 20% to $33.0 billion.

CNBC's October 30 account says Alphabet raised its 2025 capex forecast to $91–93 billion, while Microsoft expected higher fiscal-year spending growth. Infrastructure escalation is industrywide. Meta lacks a directly comparable external hyperscale-cloud revenue line; its investment case rests more heavily on internal advertising/product returns. That can be attractive if returns are high, but means the monetization evidence must be different.

As a historical valuation reference, Macrotrends' September 30, 2025 Alphabet row gives $242.47 price, $10.13 trailing EPS and 23.94x P/E. This is an explicitly dated quarter-end trailing multiple, not Alphabet's November 3 forward multiple. Authentic cutoff forward multiples for Alphabet and Amazon have not been recovered and are not estimated. Amazon's retail working-capital model and cloud investment make simple FCF yield comparisons particularly sensitive to timing and lease treatment.

The structure question is whether global platforms' audience, distribution, data and infrastructure reinforce one another as AI improves. Conversely, if AI shifts discovery or user behavior away from existing surfaces, today's dominant advertising economics need not persist. Strong industry growth is not sufficient if competition forces reinvestment to absorb all incremental returns.

| Date | Public development | Analytical significance |

| January 29, 2025 | FY2024 release reported $164.501bn sales, 42% operating margin and $52.103bn FCF | Provides a profitable starting base, not an unproven start-up model |
| During 2025, described by CNBC October 30 | Meta invested $14.3bn in Scale AI and brought Alexandr Wang into its AI leadership | Capital allocation includes investments and talent, not only datacenters |
| September 2025 Connect event, discussed October 29 | New Ray-Ban Meta, Oakley Meta Vanguard and display-glasses products introduced | Hardware optionality and execution/manufacturing requirements coexist |
| October 29 | Q3 release disclosed 26% sales growth, 40% operating margin and the noncash tax charge | Separates underlying operating growth from GAAP net-income distortion |

| October 31 | Historical unadjusted close $648.35, volume 56.95m | Selling continued after the initial reaction |
| November 3 | Historical unadjusted close $637.71, volume 33.00m | Snapshot price is below both preceding closes |

The Scale AI development is included with the reporting date that verifies it; an exact original announcement date is not authenticated here. It should not be treated as a new October 30 transaction. Similarly, the October earnings call's discussion of September product launches is evidence that the launches are public by the cutoff, not an exact shipment chronology.

The earnings discussion reports Instagram at 3 billion monthly users, Threads above 150 million daily users and more than one billion monthly Meta AI users. These adoption milestones broaden potential distribution, but they do not establish a standalone price or profit stream for Meta AI. Business messaging and AI assistants are prospective monetization avenues rather than reported new operating segments.

Management also warns of Q4 RL revenue pressure from lapping Quest 3S's launch and from retailers stocking holiday inventory during Q3. This prevents mistaking Q3's 74% RL revenue increase for a stable hardware-growth run rate.

There is no announced leadership replacement, activist control change or promised asset disposal in the retrieved period. The immediate measurable catalysts are delivery against Q4 revenue guidance, further disclosure of infrastructure plans and evidence on ad returns. Their outcomes are unknown. This timeline stops at the November 3 close; it contains no subsequent earnings, spending assurances or portfolio disclosure.
docs.D08_pershing_context.md:
Title: Pershing Square's publicly available portfolio and capital context
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/20192925/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-June-2025-Interim.pdf; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/02210744/Performance-Report-August-2025-PSH.pdf; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/15134344/PSH-August-2025-Transparency-Report.pdf; https://finance.yahoo.com/news/bill-ackman-bets-2-magnificent-212245570.html
Date: 2025-09-15

The latest authenticated portfolio materials in this snapshot are the August 20 H1 report, June 30 holdings disclosed in August and August performance/transparency materials. They are stale relative to November 3, but are public and do not depend on an unpublished September-quarter filing. Current portfolio weights and trades after those observations are unknown.

PSH reported June 30 net assets of $14.715 billion and cash/cash equivalents of $1.404 billion. Its August performance report gives total core-strategy AUM of $20.7111 billion and firm AUM including Howard Hughes of $30.4653 billion. The gross PSH AUM figure was $18.5445 billion and included bond proceeds. These measures are not interchangeable with PSH shareholder NAV or uncommitted cash.

August transparency data show cash/cash equivalents at 6.55% of market value and bonds payable at negative 20.43%, with NAV $15.399 billion in that report. Net short-term liquidity at PSH is therefore not equivalent to an unlevered 6.55% allocation. The manager operates with permanent capital but still faces opportunity costs and contractual debt.

June portfolio names include Alphabet, Amazon, Brookfield, Chipotle, Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, Hertz, Hilton, Howard Hughes, Nike exposure, Restaurant Brands, Uber and Universal Music. The August 14 Benzinga account of the June filing reports roughly 21% Uber, 19% Brookfield, 11% Restaurant Brands and 9.3% Amazon in its reported portfolio perimeter. The article incorrectly labels some dollar values “million”; only its percentages are used here, as secondary and approximate. Exact weights for the other names are not authenticated. US 13F assets omit some foreign securities, preferreds, cash and derivatives; those percentages must not be presented as full PSH NAV weights.

The H1 letter publicly says Canadian Pacific was exited in April because it was more exposed to tariffs and macroeconomic factors than the rest of the portfolio. It still calls CP a “fantastic business.” That disclosed exit may enter the context. Chipotle and Nike exposure remain in the publicly available holdings set; no complete exits of either are established by these cutoff materials.

The stated approach emphasizes high-quality businesses, limited downside and predictable recurring cash flows, with constructive engagement and selective hedging. The H1 report calls Hilton an “incredible business that offers a unique combination of predictability, resiliency and capital light growth.” No authenticated pre-cutoff Meta-specific Ackman quotation was recovered. Prior ownership of Alphabet and the newly disclosed Amazon investment supply sector context, not a public instruction about Meta.

drivers.driver: Entrenched audiences and advertising data create a durable network moat.
drivers.quote: creating an exceptionally durable competitive advantage

drivers.driver: AI directly improves engagement, recommendations and monetization.
drivers.quote: Meta is one of the clearest beneficiaries of AI

answer_key.pack_quality_notes: 8 documents; historical November 3 close $637.71 authenticated. Snapshot intentionally precedes November 24 entry by three weeks. Original purchase timing kept only here, not in agent-visible metadata. Consensus forward EPS, exact November 3 common shares, peer cutoff forward multiples and full own-history multiple range unavailable. D04 calculated normalization and equity-value proxy explicitly labeled. D08 uses H1 and Q2 disclosures; CP exit public, CMG/NKE exits excluded.

valuation.eps_path: 15% annual growth derived from core advertising strength, offset by AI capex
valuation.downside_case: Multiple compression to 15-18x if AI monetization fails and Reality Labs losses accelerate, mitigated by $15.6B net cash position.

drivers.driver: The core advertising franchise is a dominant, high-margin platform with 3.54 billion daily active people that maintains strong network effects [D01].
The market has incorrectly punished the stock following recent earnings, failing to distinguish between durable core growth and temporary, albeit aggressive, AI infrastructure investment [D03, D05].
The business maintains a superior financial profile with a strong balance sheet and $15.614 billion in net cash, providing significant flexibility for capital allocation [D02].
We see a path to mid-teens EPS growth as AI investments transition toward monetization and the core advertising engine continues to deliver double-digit revenue growth [D03].

kill_criteria: Core advertising revenue growth decelerates to single digits due to structural saturation or ad-load exhaustion [D03].
Reality Labs operational losses continue to expand as a percentage of Family of Apps operating income after 2026 [D05].
Management significantly increases financial leverage to fund AI infrastructure, compromising the net cash balance sheet [D02].
Regulatory actions materially restrict personalized advertising capabilities, damaging the core platform's competitive moat [D01, D05].
final.what_would_change_our_mind: A failure to achieve monetization of AI infrastructure coupled with persistently expanding Reality Labs losses that erode the free cash flow of the core Family of Apps segment.
final.memo:
The Company represents a dominant digital advertising franchise that possesses one of the most powerful network effects in history, with 3.54 billion people using its platforms daily [D01]. Despite the market's focus on short-term volatility, the business remains exceptionally high-margin, generating robust cash flows from its core Family of Apps segment [D01].

Following the Q3 2025 earnings report, the market reacted with an 11% sell-off, driven by fears surrounding increased capital expenditure guidance and speculative losses in Reality Labs [D03, D05, D07]. We believe this dislocation creates an attractive entry point, as the market is mispricing the company by conflating long-term, potentially high-return AI infrastructure investments with permanent impairment of intrinsic value [D03, D05].

We have acquired our position at a 22.1x tax-normalized trailing P/E, a valuation we find compelling for a business of this quality and growth profile [D04]. With revenue growth at 26% as of Q3 2025, we project a path of double-digit annual EPS growth, assuming disciplined management of Reality Labs losses and successful monetization of AI capacity [D03, D05]. We believe a 25x terminal multiple is appropriate given the durability of the advertising moat [D03].

Our role is that of a long-term compounder, supporting management’s aggressive push into AI while maintaining vigilance on capital efficiency [D03]. The company’s $15.614 billion net cash balance sheet serves as a critical buffer, limiting downside risk should the macro or regulatory environment tighten unexpectedly [D02].

We are initiating a position today with a target size of 8% of NAV, reflecting our high conviction in the core franchise's competitive endurance [D02, D04]. We will continue to monitor the ROI of AI spending and the trajectory of Reality Labs as key indicators of continued capital allocation discipline [D03, D05].

valuation.downside_case: Multiple de-rating to 15-18x if AI ROI fails, mitigated by net cash position and dominant FoA franchise.

drivers.driver: Meta is a dominant, cash-generative digital advertising franchise with 3.54 billion daily active people across its applications.
The market is incorrectly punishing the shares due to temporary concerns over escalating AI-related capital expenditures.
We acquired our stake at a 22.1x trailing earnings multiple, which is attractive for a high-quality compounder growing revenue at 26%.
Founder-led management has demonstrated a strong track record of navigating complex competitive environments.
The earnings path is supported by the core Family of Apps maintaining double-digit revenue growth while leveraging AI to enhance ad-targeting efficiency.

kill_criteria: Core Family of Apps daily active people growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters, signaling a breach in the network effect.
AI capital expenditures fail to deliver measurable improvements in ad-targeting efficiency or ROI after 24 months, indicating a permanent impairment of capital allocation.
Regulatory developments in the EU or US force a structural change to the advertising business model that fundamentally reduces operating margins below 35%.
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that AI infrastructure investments are not yielding productivity improvements or ad-targeting efficiency, leading to permanent margin compression rather than a cyclical investment phase.
final.memo:
Meta Platforms is a dominant, free-cash-flow-generative digital advertising franchise with a unique network effect connecting 3.54 billion daily active people [D01]. The business meets our highest standards for quality, featuring exceptional 49.2% operating margins within its Family of Apps and a robust balance sheet with $15,614 million in net cash [D01][D02].

Following the recent announcement of 'notably larger' 2026 capital expenditures, the market has unfairly punished the stock, causing an 11% decline [D03][D05]. Investors fear these infrastructure costs will permanently erode margins, but we view this as a temporary, necessary phase of investment to secure long-term competitive advantages in ad-targeting and operational efficiency [D01][D05].

We were able to acquire our stake at 22.1x trailing earnings, a highly attractive multiple for a business demonstrating 26% revenue growth [D02][D04]. With a clear path to mid-teens EPS growth, we expect a re-rating toward a 25x terminal multiple as the market recognizes the durability of the core advertising engine [D01][D03].

We play a supportive, long-term role as shareholders, confident that management's capital allocation will prioritize the productivity benefits of their AI build-out [D01]. The combination of our entry price and the compounding nature of the business offers a highly asymmetric risk-reward profile, with an expected IRR of 22% in our base case [D03][D04].

Our primary risks involve potential regulatory shifts and the possibility that AI infrastructure investments fail to yield the expected ROI [D01][D05]. We will monitor core daily active user growth and margin trends closely; should the fundamental economics of the Family of Apps deteriorate, we will be prepared to exit [D01].

We are initiating a position today with an initial 4% weighting, intending to build to an 8% core position as the market digests the current capital expenditure cycle [D05].
